title: Objectwise normalized scalar fibre construction
statement: Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, and a coherent continuous rational realization family $R$. Use the separated finite-type $k$-bases, their actual localized rational hearts and scalar functors, normalized geometric fibres and pullback data of [def-per-adic-fibre-comparison-data], [def-per-adic-fibre-coherence-data], [def-per-adic-normalized-fibre-data] and [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-pullback], and the actual finite scalar quotients and reduction-cone maps of [def-zl-normalized-adic-fibre-limit-data]. There exist a normalized fibre family $\omega$ and its normalized pullback $\alpha$ together with objectwise scalar components d satisfying ScalarFibreComponents [def-per-scalar-fibre-component-data]. Thus each component has the specified germ, quotient, reduction-cone and pure-tensor formulas, but no naturality or coherence in scalar embeddings is asserted.

proof.text: Use normalized fibre exactness and its intrinsic local lattice comparisons, together with the normalized pullback construction on these same intrinsic fibres. A completed-system comparison reconstructs the scalar lattice as the actual finite-free integral tensor, and realization scalar comparison fixes its degree-zero derived presentation and chart comparison.

At quotient exponent m the ramification-ceiling source power already acts by zero. The larger cofinal exponent m used by finiteScalarLevel gives the same unit and tensor quotient. Apply the finite etale stalk scalar theorem, including non-flat quotient maps, and adic tower reconstruction to identify the resulting stalk system with the quotients of the scalar tensor of the original limit.

The source stalk limit is finite free by normalized fibre exactness. In any finite basis the scalar reduction cone is a finite product of the complete target integer-ring cones, hence is limiting even in rank zero. Its inverse gives the integral iso with the prescribed completion-map equation. Localize both uniformizers and balance tensors to get each objectwise component and its local pure-tensor formula. The realization counits and finite germ formulas give the universal presentation formula. Common refinements identify these with the intrinsic fibres.
